short.title: Crocodiles in Buto's Buried Tomb #Shorts
short.hook: Scientists just found 10 mummified crocodiles - and it changes our understanding of ancient Egyptian burial practices.
script: Scientists just found 10 mummified crocodiles - and it changes our understanding of ancient Egyptian burial practices.
The site dates to approximately the 5th century B.C. near Aswan, southern Egypt.
No resin was used, and organs were left intact — a rare mummification method.
Five nearly intact bodies and five separate crocodile heads were found, including a West African species not currently found in Egypt.
Researchers believe the crocodiles were sacrificed to Sobek, god of water and fertility.
DNA analysis may confirm the presence of a now-extinct crocodile species in ancient Egypt.
Sacrificed to Sobek, or ritual for water? Or something else?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A burial site with 10 mummified crocodiles was found near Buto, Egypt, dating to around 5th century B.C. The animals were mummified without resin or organ removal, and included a West African species not native to modern Egypt. Researchers suspect they were offerings to the god Sobek. The discovery was made using satellite radar and ground-penetrating scans. Source: The Daily Galaxy, https://ua.news/en/culture/u-egipti-znaishli-pokhovannia-10-mumifikovanikh-krokodiliv-vikom-2500-rokiv
